revenue.question: Who pays Nvidia?

categories.label: Hyperscalers
categories.examples: Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta, Oracle (and frontier labs that rent from them)

categories.label: ACIE: AI clouds, industrial, enterprise
categories.examples: Neoclouds (CoreWeave, Nebius...), sovereign AI, in-house and on-premise enterprise AI

categories.label: Edge computing (incl. gaming & PC)
categories.examples: GeForce gaming, PCs, workstations, automotive, robotics

revenue.note: Hyperscale and ACIE are Data Center market platforms Nvidia began reporting in fiscal 2027; Edge Computing is the other platform. The 10-Q recast Q1 after moving one company from ACIE to Hyperscale. The reel's 51/41/8 matches the filed six-month mix (51.6/40.8/7.6).

steps.label: Cost of making chips (cost of revenue)
Gains on investments (other income, mostly equity-security gains)
steps.detail: Of 24,140 $M other income, 23,707 $M is 'gains from equity securities, net'; the remainder is interest and other items.

steps.label: Remove gains on investments
steps.why: Gains on equity securities raised profit but brought in no cash from customers. About 84% were unrealized (paper) gains; the rest came from stakes sold, whose cash is counted later as 'securities sold', not here.

steps.label: Customers owe more (receivables up)
steps.why: Sales were booked as revenue before the cash was collected.

steps.label: Inventory built up
steps.why: Cash went into chips and systems not yet sold.

steps.label: Prepayments and other assets
steps.why: Cash paid in advance, e.g. to secure supply.

steps.label: Unpaid bills, taxes owed & customer advances
steps.why: Money Nvidia owes but hasn't paid yet stays in the bank for now: supplier bills ($4.1B), accrued items such as taxes payable and customer advances ($8.0B; advances are cash already received for future deliveries), and other long-term liabilities, mostly taxes ($2.0B). The reel calls all of it 'owed to suppliers'.

steps.label: Non-cash expenses & other added back
steps.why: Stock compensation, depreciation, deferred taxes and $0.2B of other items reduced profit without using cash.

cfo.note: The source's rounded line items sum to 0.41, not 0.42. Unrounded filed values sum to 0.4185; the 1-cent gap is rounding and is shown as a labelled residual.

sources_of_cash.label: Borrowing (bond issuance)
sources_of_cash.why: $25B of senior notes issued in Q2. Borrowed cash must be repaid; it is not earnings.

sources_of_cash.label: Securities sold (net)
sources_of_cash.why: Equity securities sold ($7.2B, gross) plus debt securities sold or matured net of purchases ($4.8B). That's converting assets into cash, not revenue. Note the mix: equity sales are gross here while equity purchases (24 cents) are gross on the other side, so net new equity investment was about 20 cents.

uses_of_cash.label: Kept or spent on itself
uses_of_cash.why: A residual. In the filing it's capex ($4.4B), taxes paid on employee stock awards ($4.5B, which works much like a buyback), a $2.9B Groq payment, other items, and an $11.8B rise in cash on hand. It's not all spending.

uses_of_cash.label: Invested into the AI ecosystem
uses_of_cash.why: Purchases of equity securities ($42.4B), the cash leg of new investments.

cash.note: 'New cash' is the source's construct: operating cash + borrowing + securities sold. It is not a GAAP subtotal. The 13-cent 'kept' figure is calculated as the residual.

bridge_filed.label: Valuation change & other (calculated residual)
bridge_filed.detail: Residual 23,757 $M is close to the reported 23,707 $M of equity-security gains.

close_mix_source.label: Supply chain (parts & tools)
close_mix_source.note: About 70% Intel (source; not confirmed in filings).

portfolio.note: The filing does not name investees. The category mix is the source's estimate. The source's '10 cents of appreciation' is a net figure: about 13 cents of valuation gains less about 4 cents of equity sold.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.rel: Equity investment + residual-value guarantees on its Ohio leases
companies.amount: $30B equity pledge paid in tranches (final $10B reported Oct 2026; amount funded by Jul 26 not disclosed); guarantees capped at $105B (Aug 2026, not yet effective)

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.amount: Up to $10B (per a reported Huang remark; timing of funding not confirmed in filings)

companies.name: Intel
companies.amount: $5B common stock purchase, completed; source says ~70% of supply-chain holdings

companies.name: Marvell
companies.rel: Equity investment (makes ASICs for Nvidia's competitors)

companies.name: CoreWeave
companies.rel: Equity + capacity agreements (Nvidia rents back compute)

companies.name: SB Energy
companies.rel: Equity + developer of the guaranteed Ohio campus

filed_items.label: Equity investment commitments
filed_items.note: Agreed future equity checks to AI model makers, infrastructure financiers and other private companies, subject to contingencies.

filed_items.label: Cloud compute Nvidia buys for its own R&D
filed_items.note: Cloud service agreements. Per the 10-Q they 'provide the cloud infrastructure to support our research and development of our open models' and autonomous-vehicle software. That's Nvidia's own spending, not support for anyone else. The reel's $1.23 is only reproduced if this is included.

filed_items.label: AI cloud agreements (capacity backstops)
filed_items.note: Multi-year agreements with AI cloud partners. Nvidia may earn a share of revenue from supported capacity and bears risk if the clouds can't sell it.

filed_items.label: Leases Nvidia signed, to reassign to third parties
filed_items.note: Nvidia is the lessee on these ~15-year leases (commencing FY2028-29) and expects to hand them to third parties. If it can't, it keeps the cost.

filed_items.label: Land, power & shell guarantees for AI clouds
filed_items.note: Maximum gross exposure on AI cloud partners' data center leases. May overlap economically with the AI cloud agreements above.

filed_items.label: SB Energy / OpenAI Ohio lease & power-payment guarantees
filed_items.note: Credit-support guarantees (reported in the press as residual-value guarantees), capped at $105B on defined portions of lease and power payments for ~4.25 GW of IT load. Each guarantee takes effect only when its lease starts. Amounts step up over nine construction phases (first expected FY2029) and decline over each 20-year lease. Ends on a tenant credit-rating event. OpenAI agreed to indemnify Nvidia for certain losses. Pays only if the tenant defaults. No guarantee is effective yet, though the 10-Q reports the full $105B as maximum gross exposure. Signed Aug 2026, after the period end.

source_mix.label: Frontier labs
source_mix.note: 89% of it is the $105B Ohio guarantee (source); 105/117 = 0.90 (calculated).

source_mix.label: Neoclouds (capacity backstops, credit support, equity in lending vehicles)
Supply chain, apps & physical AI (unresolved remainder)
source_mix.note: 1.23 - 0.66 - 0.52. The whiteboard shows a 2-cent apps block; the rest is not legible.

expected_outflow.note: Neither the source nor the filing gives an expected payout. Guarantees pay only on default and only the shortfall, so expected cash outflow is likely far below the gross cap, but it cannot be quantified here.

commitments.note: We found a combination of filed items that sums to the reel's $1.23 ($218.5B = $1.229). The reel never gave its breakdown, so this is our inference. It reaches $1.23 only by counting $29B of cloud compute Nvidia buys for its own R&D. Without that, ecosystem commitments and guarantees are $189.5B ($1.07). It mixes a July 26 period-end note with guarantees signed in August.

layers.label: Investment holdings (market or carrying value, Jul 2026)
Illustrative residual-value support under $500B financing MOUs
layers.note: Illustrative only: 25% x $500B = $125B. Nvidia disclosed no total cap. It 'may provide' support for up to 25% of an opportunity, case by case. The MOUs are non-binding, and the $500B+ is capital the partners hope to raise over time.

exposure.guardrail: These layers can't simply be added together. Holdings are assets Nvidia owns, valued at a point in time (and including gains). Commitments and guarantees are gross caps that may never be paid, and some may overlap. The MOU figure is an illustration based on non-binding agreements. None of it is debt, cash already spent, or an expected loss. All of it is compared to just six months of sales. Against annualized sales each cent figure would be roughly half (about 0.6x against the actual trailing-twelve-month revenue).

lehman.source_claim: Compared to Lehman at 32 to one gross leverage, I think we're okay.
lehman.why_not_comparable: Bank leverage is total assets / shareholders' equity, and Lehman's assets were funded mostly with borrowed money. The reel's 2.49 is (assets + gross promise caps + an illustrative figure) / six months of revenue. Different numerator, different denominator. Measured the way Lehman's was, Nvidia's leverage on Jul 26, 2026 was 1.4x ($320.3B assets / $229.0B equity).

claims.claim: $1 = Nvidia sales in 'the first six months of 2026'
claims.finding: The scale matches Nvidia's fiscal first half of FY27 (Jan 26 - Jul 26, 2026): $177.8B of revenue. That's a fiscal half, not a calendar half.
Matches the 10-Q's six-month market-platform table: 51.6 / 40.8 / 7.6 (after Nvidia recast Q1). 'Gaming & PC' sits inside Edge Computing, which also covers auto and robotics.
10-Q: costs 34.1, other income 13.6 (13.3 is equity gains), tax 13.2, net income 66.4. Operating profit is also ~66c; the gains and taxes happen to cancel.
$74.4B = 41.8c. The reel's rounded items sum to 41c (rounding).

claims.claim: Borrowed 14c, sold 7c of securities, 63c new cash
claims.finding: $24.9B of notes = 14.0c. Equity sold (gross) plus debt securities (net) = 6.8c. 'New cash' is the reel's own construct, not a GAAP subtotal.
Buybacks + dividends = 25.5c; gross equity purchases = 23.8c (about 20c net of stakes sold). The 13c is a residual (capex, employee-stock taxes, Groq, cash build).
Equity holdings grew from $40.0B (22.5c) to $98.9B (55.6c), at market or carrying value.
A net figure: valuation change of about 13.4c, less about 4.1c of equity sold.

claims.claim: Vast majority of new 24c was one $30B OpenAI investment
claims.finding: The $30B was a pledge paid in tranches; a final $10B tranche was reported in Oct 2026. If that came after Jul 26, only about $20B (11c) is in the six-month purchases, and the rest sits in equity commitments. The filing doesn't say.

claims.claim: Intel ~70% of supply-chain holdings; CoreWeave half of neocloud exposure; OpenAI over half of labs
claims.finding: The filing names no investees. Plausible from announced stakes, but not confirmable.

claims.claim: $1.23 of credit and equity support promised
claims.finding: A combination of filed items sums to $218.5B (122.9c), but only if $29B of cloud compute Nvidia buys for its own R&D is counted. Excluding it, ecosystem commitments and guarantees are $189.5B (106.6c).

claims.claim: $105B credit guarantee backing OpenAI's 9.2 GW, half-trillion-dollar Ohio data center
claims.finding: The $105B cap is verified: residual-value guarantees, Aug 2026, on ~4.25 GW of IT load with an option for ~3.8 GW more. They aren't effective until leases start (first phase expected FY2029). 9.2 GW may be total facility power, and the 'half trillion' wasn't confirmed; neither is in the filing.

claims.claim: August: six financiers + Nvidia agreed to finance $500B+, up to 25% residual support = 70c
claims.finding: The Aug 10, 2026 MOUs are non-binding. The $500B+ is a target for third-party capital. 'Up to 25% of an opportunity' applies case by case, with no total cap disclosed. 25% x $500B = $125B (70.3c) is illustrative.

claims.claim: $1.79 invested or promised; up to $2.49 on the hook
claims.finding: The arithmetic holds, but it adds owned assets (including gains), gross caps that may overlap, and an illustrative figure, all measured against six months of sales.
Lehman reported 30.7x (Nov 2007) and 31.7x (Feb 2008), assets / equity. Nvidia measured the same way: 1.4x. The reel's 2.49 is a different ratio altogether.

claims.claim: Nvidia 'looks more like a venture capital or hedge fund'
claims.finding: This is the reel's interpretation, not an accounting classification. Nvidia reports as a semiconductor company. Its equity holdings are about 31% of total assets.
